item.title: Local members call for Fianna Fáil review to be published
item.description: Local Fianna Fáil members have expressed their frustration as a review into the party's botched presidential campaign has been delayed further. Jim Gavin's legal team has requested a copy of the review before it's published. The Taoiseach informed his Fianna Fáil parliamentary party of the delay last night. item.title: Multimillion-euro Connolly Barracks hub a big boost for community groups
item.description: The cathaoirleach of Longford Municipal District says the overhaul of Connolly Barracks will be a huge boost to community groups. The historic building shut down in 2009 and is being converted into a cultural and community hub. The project has secured €7 million in funding, and it will be complete in two years’ time. item.description: The revelation comes as a local TD highlighted the lack of any emergency accommodation for women and children fleeing domestic abuse. item.title: Free Christmas dinner and music in Boyle on December 28th
item.description: A free Christmas dinner event is taking place in Boyle on December 28th. It’s on in Dorothy Shannon’s King House Tea Rooms, for the eighth time. To book your place, drop into the coffee shop or call 087-6430326. Advertisement Dorothy says the event gets busier every year and Christmas is a lonely time for many people.

item.title: Ireland West Airport funding a major boost for region, says local Minister
item.description: A local Minister of State has welcomed significant funding of Ireland West Airport. Minister for Further Education Marian Harkin says a major boost to regional development. The Sligo-Leitrim TD was speaking after the airport was awarded €1.9 million in Government funding. It's part of an overall package of €4 million announced today by the Minister for Transport, Darragh O’Brien. item.title: Calls for greater investment in south Leitrim water infrastructure
item.description: The Dáil has heard the need for greater water infrastructure in south Leitrim. Significant outages have impacted many areas including Cloone, Carrigallen and Aughnasheelin. It's felt this is due to the plant being over capacity. Local TD Martin Kenny says it's a part of a wider problem nationally in terms of waste water. item.title: Elphin Credit Union to close following structural damage
item.description: Roscommon Credit Union Ltd has announced the closure of its Elphin branch after significant structural damage to the building rendered continued operations unsustainable. The decision was communicated to members in a letter issued on Wednesday, outlining the circumstances and detailing the supports that will remain available. item.title: Leitrim councillor opposes 30km/h speed limit in towns
item.description: A Leitrim councillor says he wouldn't be in favour of 30 kilometre per hour speed limits in towns. The Department of Transport directed local authorities to begin reviewing speed limits on roads in built-up and urban areas earlier this year. Councils will introduce lower limits where appropriate, including new 30 kilometre per hour zones in towns and cities. item.title: Not enough enforcement of child ban on e-scooters - Scahill
item.description: A Roscommon senator is calling for more garda enforcement of the ban on children using e-scooters. These vehicles have been legal on Irish roads since May 2024 - but kids under 16 can't use them. Fine Gael senator Gareth Scahill raised concerns about the issue in the Seanad. item.title: Denis Naughten joins public relations firm Red Flag
item.description: Former Roscommon TD Denis Naughten has joined public-relations and strategic communications firm, Red Flag Consulting, in an advisory role. Mr Naughten, who served for many years as a TD, was first elected in 1997. He was minister for communications, climate action and environment from 2016 to 2018 before leaving politics at the end of last year. Advertisement Red Flag Consulting, which is run by Deirdre Grant and Karl Brophy, said Mr Naughten will advise its clients across a range of industries
